files.s: In this file we define `Real.logb` to be the logarithm of a real number in a given base `b`. We define this as the division of the natural logarithms of the argument and the base, so that we have a globally defined function with `logb b 0 = 0`, `logb b (-x) = logb b x`, `logb 0 x = 0`, and `logb (-b) x = logb b x`.

h.d: Induction principle for intervals of real numbers: if a proposition `P` is true on `[x₀, r * x₀)` and if `P` for `[x₀, r^n * x₀)` implies `P` for `[r^n * x₀, r^(n+1) * x₀)`, then `P` is true for all `x ≥ x₀`.
The real logarithm base b is continuous as a function from positive reals.
The real logarithm base b is continuous as a function from nonzero reals.
The function `|logb b x|` tends to `+∞` as `x` tendsto `+∞`. See also `tendsto_logb_atTop` and `tendsto_logb_atTop_of_base_lt_one`.
The real logarithm in a given base. As with the natural logarithm, we define `logb b x` to be `logb b |x|` for `x < 0`, and `0` for `x = 0`.

files.s: In this file we define `Real.log` to be the logarithm of a real number. As usual, we extend it from its domain `(0, +∞)` to a globally defined function. We choose to do it so that `log 0 = 0` and `log (-x) = log x`.

h.d: The real logarithm is continuous as a function from positive reals.
The real logarithm is continuous as a function from nonzero reals.
The real logarithm function tends to `+∞` at `+∞`.
Bound for `|log x * x|` in the interval `(0, 1]`.
See `Real.one_sub_inv_le_log_of_pos` for the stronger version when `x ≠ 0`.
See `Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos` for the stronger version when `x ≠ 0`.

files.t: Derivative and series expansion of real logarithm
files.s: In this file we prove that `Real.log` is infinitely smooth at all nonzero `x : ℝ`. We also prove that the series `∑' n : ℕ, x ^ (n + 1) / (n + 1)` converges to `(-Real.log (1 - x))` for all `x : ℝ`, `|x| < 1`.

h.d: Expansion of `log (1 + a)` as a series in powers of `a / (a + 2)`.
Expansion of `log (1 + a⁻¹)` as a series in powers of `1 / (2 * a + 1)`.
Power series expansion of `log(1 + x) - log(1 - x)` for `|x| < 1`.
Power series expansion of the logarithm around `1`.
For `0 ≤ x < 1`, the partial sums of the series expansion of $\frac{1}{2} * \log(\frac{1+x}{1-x})$ at `0` form a lower bound for it.

A lemma estimating the difference between $\frac{1}{2} * \log(\frac{1+x}{1-x})$ and its Taylor series at `0`, where the bound tends to `0`. This bound is particularly useful for explicit estimates of logarithms.

files.s: We define `log` as an extension of the logarithm of a positive real to the extended nonnegative reals `ℝ≥0∞`. The function takes values in the extended reals `EReal`, with `log 0 = ⊥` and `log ⊤ = ⊤`.

h.d: The extension of the real logarithm to `ℝ≥0∞`.
`log` is increasing;
, `ENNReal.log_surjective`, `ENNReal.log_bijective`: `log` is injective, surjective, and bijective;
, `ENNReal.log_pow`, `ENNReal.log_rpow`: `log` satisfies the identities `log (x * y) = log x + log y` and `log (x ^ y) = y * log x` (with either `y ∈ ℕ` or `y ∈ ℝ`).

The logarithm function defined on the extended nonnegative reals `ℝ≥0∞` to the extended reals `EReal`. Coincides with the usual logarithm function and with `Real.log` on positive reals, and takes values `log 0 = ⊥` and…

files.t: Properties of the extended logarithm and exponential
files.s: We prove that `log` and `exp` define order isomorphisms between `ℝ≥0∞` and `EReal`.

h.d: The order isomorphism between `ℝ≥0∞` and `EReal` defined by `log` and `exp`.
The order isomorphism between `EReal` and `ℝ≥0∞` defined by `exp` and `log`.
`log` as a homeomorphism.
`exp` as a homeomorphism.
, `ENNReal.exp_log`: `log` and `exp` are inverses of each other.
, `EReal.exp_mul`: `exp` satisfies the identities `exp (n * x) = (exp x) ^ n` and `exp (x * y) = (exp x) ^ y`.

files.s: We define `exp` as an extension of the exponential of a real to the extended reals `EReal`. The function takes values in the extended nonnegative reals `ℝ≥0∞`, with `exp ⊥ = 0` and `exp ⊤ = ⊤`.

h.d: The extension of the real exponential to `EReal`.
`exp` is increasing;
, `EReal.exp_add`: `exp` satisfies the identities `exp (-x) = (exp x)⁻¹` and `exp (x + y) = exp x * exp y`.

files.t: Multiplicative inverse and iteration of real logarithm
files.s: We prove properties of the functions `x ↦ (log x)⁻¹` and `x ↦ log (log x)`.

h.d: gives a formula for the derivative of `x ↦ (log x)⁻¹` which holds for all values.
gives a formula for the derivative of `x ↦ log (log x)` which holds for all values.

files.s: In this file we describe the tonality of the logarithm function when multiplied by functions of the form `x ^ a`.

files.t: The functions `x ↦ x * log x` and `x ↦ - x * log x`
files.s: The purpose of this file is to record basic analytic properties of - `x ↦ x * log x`, called `mul_log` in theorem statements - `x ↦ - x * log x`, named `negMulLog`, which is notably used in the theory of Shannon entropy.

h.d: the function `x ↦ - x * log x` from `ℝ` to `ℝ`.
Not differentiable, hence `deriv` has junk value zero.
At `x=0`, `(fun x ↦ x * log x)` is not differentiable (but note that it is continuous, see `continuous_mul_log`).

files.t: The Positive Part of the Logarithm
files.s: This file defines the function `Real.posLog = r ↦ max 0 (log r)` and introduces the notation `log⁺`. For a finite length-`n` sequence `f i` of reals, it establishes the following standard estimates.

h.d: Multiplying the argument of `log⁺` by a nonzero factor `x` changes its value by at most `log⁺ x + log⁺ x⁻¹`, which equals `|log x|` by `Real.abs_log_eq_posLog_add_posLog_inv`.
Variant of `posLog_add` for norms of elements in normed additive commutative groups, using monotonicity of `log⁺` and the triangle inequality.
Estimate for `log⁺` of a sum. See `Real.posLog_sum` for a variant involving multiple summands.
Variant of `posLog_sum` for norms of elements in normed additive commutative groups, using monotonicity of `log⁺` and the triangle inequality.
Estimate for `log⁺` of a sum. See `Real.posLog_add` for a variant involving just two summands.
Estimate for `log⁺` of a product. See `Real.posLog_mul` for a variant with only two factors.

files.t: The logarithm as a limit of powers
files.s: This file shows that the logarithm can be expressed as a limit of powers, namely that `p⁻¹ * (x ^ p - 1)` tends to `log x` as `p` tends to zero for positive `x`.

files.t: Bounds on the partial sums of the logarithm
files.s: The partial sum `∑ n ∈ Finset.Ioc 0 N, Real.log n` equals `Real.log N !`. Comparing the sum with the integral `∫ t in 1..x, Real.log t = x * log x - x + 1` yields crude upper and lower bounds of the form `∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 ⌊x⌋₊, log n = x * log x - x + O(log x)`, which are convenient in analytic number theory (for instance in the proof of Mertens' theorems).

h.d: `∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 N, log n = log N !`, and its `Finset.range` restatement `sum_log_add_one_eq_log_factorial`: `∑ n ∈ range N, log (n + 1) = log N !`.
/ `le_sum_log`: two-sided bounds on `∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 ⌊x⌋₊, log n`.
a sharper lower bound `N * log N - N ≤ ∑ n ∈ Ioc 0 N, log n` via Stirling.
An even cruder lower bound on the partial sum of the logarithm.
A crude lower bound on the partial sum of the logarithm.
An even cruder upper bound on the partial sum of the logarithm.

files.s: We give conditions under which the logarithms of a summable sequence are summable. We also use this to relate summability of `f` to multipliability of `1 + f`.

h.d: In a complete normed ring, `∏' i, (1 + f i)` is convergent if the sum of real numbers `∑' i, ‖f i‖` is convergent.
The exponential of a convergent sum of real logs is the corresponding infinite product.
Alternate version of `Real.multipliable_of_summable_log` assuming only that positivity holds eventually.
The exponential of a convergent sum of complex logs is the corresponding infinite product.
